drivers.lead: Hamilton drew level with Schumacher's seven in the wet at Istanbul in 2020, sixteen years after Schumacher had set it
drivers.note: Michael Schumacher reached seven in 2004, five of them consecutive from 2000, and the mark stood alone for sixteen seasons. Lewis Hamilton equalled it with a race to spare in a Turkish Grand Prix he started sixth and won by twenty-five seconds. Neither has added one since — Schumacher's last was 2004, Hamilton's 2020. The routes were not alike: Schumacher won his first two with Benetton in 1994 and 1995 and the other five with Ferrari, while Hamilton took 2008 with McLaren and six with Mercedes. Juan Manuel Fangio's five, won between 1951 and 1957 with four different manufacturers, has been third on the list since the year it was set. What makes seven hard now is that the sport's longest recent run stopped at four: Max Verstappen won 2021 to 2024 and would need three more, and 2025 produced a first-time champion in Lando Norris.

teams.lead: Ferrari's sixteenth came in 2008, and McLaren's back-to-back in 2024 and 2025 has taken second place to ten
teams.note: The sixteen run from 1961 to 2008 and include six in a row between 1999 and 2004, which was the record for consecutive constructors' titles until Mercedes won eight straight from 2014 to 2021. Ferrari has entered every constructors' championship since the award was created in 1958, and it has now gone seventeen seasons without one — longer than the run that built the record. McLaren is the only team currently closing the gap. Its 2024 title was a first since 1998 and the 2025 one, sealed with six rounds still to run, was its first successful defence since 1991. Behind them the chase has stalled: Williams has nine and none since 1997, Lotus seven and none since 1978. Six more would put McLaren level, which on the last two seasons is not absurd, but it is still six more.
